title: One question per card
hook: A card asking three things can hide which one you missed.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Split a compound prompt into separately checkable cues.

objective: Split a compound prompt into separately checkable cues.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: A card asking three things can hide which one you missed. Which card makes a missed item identifiable? Correct option: One target per cue. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred.

claims.text: Separate cues expose separate gaps. A correct answer to one cue does not establish knowledge of the other two.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: recall. One short reconstruction; not a retention experiment. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, one-question-one-card fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three.
